messages:
Sarah M.: heads up — after last night's runtime deploy we're seeing a regression on multi-GPU TP+PP runs. 8-GPU node jobs (2x4 mesh) showing steady 15–40% higher p50 token latency when sequence length spikes >1024. Noticed this on NVLink-connected nodes and on PCIe-only nodes, but symptoms differ.
Jamie C.: seeing the same on our tests. p95 blips up to 2.5x during long-context evals. repro with `rosetta_longseq_v2` harness.
Amit R.: quick datapoint from profiling: allreduce microbench shows intra-node NVLink allreduce ~0.9ms, PCIe peer copy ~2.8ms, cross-node EFA ~3.4ms. But the regression mostly correlates with an extra kernel fallback we added last week (kernelselect v3).
Lena T.: can you paste the kernelselect decision log? curious if it's falling back to non-fused GEMM for certain seq_len/batch combos.
Sarah M.: pasted snippet below — the runtime now logs the rule that triggered: 
```
[2026-03-17T03:12:02Z] kernelselect: model=rwkv-32b, seq=1536, tp=2, pp=2 -> selected=kern_fallback_matmul (reason=kv-prefetch-unavailable, heur_score=-1)
[2026-03-17T03:12:02Z] batching: inferred batch_window=12ms -> slice=3 (forced_synchronous=false)
[2026-03-17T03:12:02Z] kvcache: hit_rate=87% -> prefetch_queue_len=0 (evicted_prefixes=3)
```
Amit R.: kern_fallback_matmul is the slower path — it disables our fused attention path that overlaps compute+comm for KV fetch. If kv-prefetch-unavailable is being triggered, maybe the KV eviction policy is too aggressive for long seqs.
Jamie C.: interesting — on NVLink nodes the slowdown looks like CPU-side queuing while waiting for allreduce to finish; on PCIe nodes it's dominated by the memcpy step. Kernel fallback amplifies both because it increases compute time and reduces comm overlap.
Lena T.: hypothesis: when seq > 1024 and batch_window < 15ms our batching heuristics slice requests smaller which increases per-step allreduce frequency and prevents efficient pipelining. Combined with prefetch misses, we get serialized fetch+allreduce+compute.
Sarah M.: repro commands I used: 
```bash
./run_eval --model rwkv-32b --tp 2 --pp 2 --seq 1536 --batch-size 1 --profile=comm,kv,kernelselect
```
Output summary: allreduce instantaneous times spike from 1.0ms -> 4.1ms at runtime step 26, kernel time increases by ~30% after fallback.
Amit R.: attaching brief flame: comm stalls line up with `KV_FETCH` ops; we observed multiple concurrent attempts to prefetch the same prefix, causing lock contention in kvcache manager. That explains prefetch_queue_len=0 while evictions climb.
Jamie C.: possible immediate mitigations: 1) revert the last kernelselect rule that forces fallback on kv-prefetch-unavailable, 2) raise batch_window threshold for long-seq traces so we reduce slices, 3) tweak kvcache LRU to prefer recent prefixes during long-seq workloads.
Lena T.: I can try (2) quickly — increasing batch_window reduces slice count and should allow more compute/comm overlap. I'll run a canary on a single 8-GPU NVLink node.
Sarah M.: thanks. Amit, can you gather a microtrace of the kvcache evictions + prefetch logs for the failing run and dump into /tmp/trace-1973500000.json? add timestamps.
Amit R.: on it. I'll also run ring vs tree allreduce microbench with our current comm scheduler; want to know if switching to tree for large payloads helps (trade-off: more messages but lower critical path for reduce).
Jamie C.: FYI deploy rollback might be noisy for running long jobs — prefer config flip if possible. infra-bot, can we open a canary config and pin a single node pool with batch_window=20ms for tests?
infra-bot: created canary config `kernelselect-canary-1973500000` on pool `nvlink-canary-4x2`. TTL=2h.
Lena T.: running canary now. initial numbers look promising: p50 down ~12% on NVLink for seq=1536 after raising batch_window to 20ms. p95 still has spikes but fewer.
Sarah M.: good signal. Next steps: Lena to complete canary and share logs; Amit to upload kvcache microtrace; Jamie to prepare a rollback plan for the kernelselect rule if canary fails; I'll coordinate a broader test matrix covering PCIe-only nodes and cross-node EFA.
Jamie C.: noted. I'll also add a quick experiment: try `allreduce=tree` for seq>1024 payloads to see if that reduces worst-case latency.
Amit R.: uploaded /tmp/trace-1973500000.json and a short script to parse it: 
```python
# kvcache_eviction_summary.py
# prints prefix eviction timeline + prefetch attempts
```
Sarah M.: thanks. leaving this thread open while we validate. please add brief one-line updates here as you get numbers. :eyes:
Lena T.: canary finished — attaching CSV in #eng-runtime-artifacts. p50 improved on NVLink; PCIe-only still 18% reg.
Jamie C.: tree-allreduce experiment reduced peak allreduce from 4.1ms -> 2.2ms on cross-node EFA for large payloads. looks promising but increases aggregate network messages ~1.3x.
Amit R.: conclusion from my trace: kvcache LRU churn triggered by concurrent prefetchers + small batch windows. short-term fix: increase batch window + disable the kv-prefetch-unavailable fallback. medium-term: add per-prefix in-flight suppression to prevent duplicate prefetches.
Sarah M.: great, plan: (A) flip canary to include tree-allreduce for seq>1024, (B) patch kernelselect to skip fallback when prefetch misses are transient, (C) schedule follow-up to prototype per-prefix suppression. I'll open a GH issue with action items.
Jamie C.: +1. I'll PR the tree-allreduce toggle behind a flag.
Lena T.: logging an ETA: canary data + PRs by EOD.
Sarah M.: thanks team. :thumbsup:
